resources.string: Orbit turns the buttons you already have (earbuds, the volume keys on the phone, a Bluetooth remote, keyboard or game pad, the CMF Buds Pro 2 dial, a tap on the back of the phone) into a controller: open a wheel of tools, move to pick one, select it; your buttons then scroll, zoom, change brightness, switch apps or take photos. This service draws the wheel on screen and performs those actions (scroll gestures, zoom, back/home/recents, screenshots, opening apps). It also sees presses of hardware buttons (volume keys, remotes, keyboards, game pads) so that the buttons you add as a controller can drive Orbit instead of their usual action; other buttons pass through untouched, and which keys you press is never recorded. It only acts when you use your controls. It does not read or store the content of your screen, with two exceptions: the name of the app in front, to offer recent apps in the Apps tool, and, only when you press Select with the Camera or Teleprompter tool, the buttons of the app in front, to find and press its shutter or play / pause. Nothing is stored or sent anywhere.
